findings.title: Seated coworkers hover in mid-air when their chair is taken or knocked away
findings.problem: Big Meeting seats 22 of its 24 coworkers on task chairs. The chairs are ordinary dynamic props, and the prompt next to every desk is "Grab the chair". A seated blob is not attached to its chair. It is a static group at the chair's spawn spot with its body lifted 0.35 m (`seated?.35:0`). When Pip grabs the chair, or a throw or cable drag knocks it away, the blob stays at 0.35 m and floats over bare floor: its capsule bottom sits about 0.40 m up, with nothing under it (characters-51, -52, -52b). Grabbing or wrecking chairs is one of the first things a Good Job-style player does in an office. The result reads as a broken model, not a joke, and it happens at every one of the 22 desks. A coworker falling on their bum, or popping up to stand with the alarm pose, would be a free laugh (DR-03, DR-04).
evidence: src/game.ts:134 (baseY fixed at spawn; no link to the chair prop)
src/levels/meeting.ts:15-18 (chair prop and npc pushed at the same x,z; chair is a normal grabbable prop)
findings.fix: In src/game.ts, give each seated Npc a `chair?:Prop` reference when it is built in addNpc. Pick the nearest `kind==='chair'` prop within 0.3 m of the NpcSpot, the same way `desk` is found on line 133. In render(), each frame, compare the chair's body translation with npc.group.position. If the chair is more than 0.35 m away horizontally, or tilted more than 25° (from its quaternion), or is `this.held`, set `npc.seated=false`, ease `npc.baseY` to 0 over about 0.25 s with a squash on landing (reuse the `duck` scale), call `this.alarm(npc.group.position,1.5)`, and play the 'alarm' voice. That gives the "fell off the chair" gag. Optionally, when the chair comes back within 0.4 m, sit again (baseY back to 0.35, snapping to the chair's x,z). A cheaper alternative: make occupied chairs fixed or kinematic and leave them out of nearest().
findings.verify: Retake characters-50/51/52 with mockups/review5/tools/characters/s7.mjs (grab the chair at (-6.85,-7.05), walk away). The blob must land on the floor or stand, and none may hover. Add a spec to tests/routes.spec.ts: grab that chair, advance(1), then assert that no npc group has body y > 0.05 without a chair under it. That needs a snapshot field such as `npcs:[{seated,y}]`.
findings.verify_reason: Reproduced it myself. In meeting I grabbed the chair beside (-6.85,-7.05) with E, carried it away, dropped it and orbited at zoom 9. The blue glasses-and-tie blob hangs in the air with no chair under it, and its shadow lies well clear of its base (verify-characters-05, -05b). Code agrees: src/game.ts:128 sets body.position.y=.35 when seated, the npc group is a plain T.Group at the spawn x,z with no link to the chair prop, and src/game.ts:429 rewrites body y from the fixed baseY every frame. One correction: Meeting has 26 NPCs, of which 24 are seated (20 at desks plus 4 in the boardroom, src/levels/meeting.ts:4,19,26), not '22 of 24'. P1 holds: this is the first office room, chair-grabbing is an early Good Job verb, and the result reads as broken rather than as a joke.
extra_evidence: src/levels/meeting.ts:19 (npcs pushed only while length<22, so 20 desk NPCs) and :26 (4 boardroom NPCs on dynamic chairs)
findings.fix_correction: The main fix (find the chair at build time, and in render() drop or pop the blob up when the chair moves more than 0.35 m, tilts, or is held) is right. Don't take the 'cheaper alternative' of fixed or kinematic chairs left out of nearest(). It removes grabbable clutter from a dense physics room, which goes against the Good Job chaos rule. snapshot() (src/game.ts:504) also has no npc field yet, so the proposed spec needs `npcs:this.npcs.map(n=>({seated:n.seated,y:+n.body.position.y.toFixed(2)}))` added there.

findings.title: REGRESSION-check DR-73 still open: the cable runs through Pip's legs and body when holding the plug, at the win push-in, and on the Lunch thick cable
findings.problem:
The cable's last point is Pip's glove (handPosition → rig.hand under the right elbow). The rope solver never treats Pip's body as an obstacle, so whenever the reel is behind or beside Pip, the hose runs straight from the glove down through his leg or hip to the floor:
- Playground idle hold, back view: the hose crosses the right leg (characters-19, third panel).
- Lunch: the striped thick cable falls from the glove through both thighs (characters-77).
- Playground win push-in, the hero shot: the gold connected lead and plug lie under and through Pip's right boot (characters-64b).

R2 bug 3 (P3 in the earlier checklist) is not fixed. The cable is the star (AGENTS 4), and in the moment it is most on show it clips through the hero. Related: on the first F at the Lunch dolly, the right mitt pushes into the reel drum (characters-75), and the dolly then parks against Pip's hip (characters-76; DR-74's 1.3 m follow distance).
evidence: src/game.ts:293 (cable end = hand; no body clearance)
src/render/pipRig.ts:40 (hand at elbow + (.04,-.33,.04), right side only)
findings.fix: 1) In drawCable (src/game.ts:290-305) and the Lunch cable draw, add a short Pip-clearance leg before the hand: insert a point 0.45 m behind Pip at hip height (p.y-.2, offset by -heading), and when the previous rope point is in front of Pip, insert one at the side of the hand instead. Simplest version: treat Pip as a vertical capsule (r .38, y 0..1.4) and push any interpolated hose sample that falls inside it out radially before building hoseGeometry. 2) In pipRig.ts:75, when holdingPlug, turn the right forearm so the lead leaves the glove backwards (elbow x +.3), so the tube naturally trails behind the hip. 3) At plug-in (the win), set the plug's end segment to come off the socket away from Pip, and move Pip 0.5 m back from the socket before the push-in. For the Lunch dolly, use a follow distance of at least 2 m (src/lunch-runtime.ts:237), as DR-74 asks.
findings.verify: Retake characters-19 (s2.mjs), characters-64b (s8.mjs) and characters-77 (s9.mjs). No hose pixels may overlap Pip's legs or boots. Optionally, check in the specs that every rope point stays more than 0.35 m horizontally from the player except the final hand point.
findings.verify_reason: Confirmed in code: drawCable ends the hose at handPosition() (src/game.ts:289,293), and nothing pushes cable samples out of Pip's body. The cited screenshots, though, show the hose overlapping Pip in screen projection, not provably going through him. In characters-19 panel 3 and characters-77 the hose runs between the camera and the legs. My own plug-hold captures from three angles (verify-characters-18 sheet) show the lead leaving the glove sideways and going behind the torso, without a clear penetration. The glove sits about 0.43 m out to the side, and the legs reach only to x≈±0.29, so a hose trailing straight back clears the leg. Clipping should happen when the reel is diagonally behind on the far side, but no screenshot shows that unambiguously. In 64b the gold lead lies on the floor under the boot, which is a minor ground-level overlap. DR-73 lists this as Known, with P3 in the source. It is polish, not a fun or teaching blocker, so P2.
findings.fix_correction: Do part 1 (push hose samples out of a capsule of r≈0.38 around Pip, y 0–1.4, before hoseGeometry) in src/game.ts drawCable and the Lunch cable draw. Skip part 3 (moving Pip 0.5 m back from the socket at the win): it changes plug-in reach and the tested coordinates for a cosmetic gain. Setting the dolly follow distance to 2 m or more (src/lunch-runtime.ts, the `d>1.3` check in the thick-cable follow) is DR-74's fix, which is separate and fine.

findings.title: Sprint makes the feet skate about 50% and the steps get slower than walking; slow hauling also slides
findings.problem:
The rig ties step phase to distance so that planted feet don't skate (pipRig.ts:49-52), but the stride formula only matches at normal walking speed. From the code's own numbers (leg about 0.56–0.59 m, swingAmp = .32 + .26·amount + .12·run, cycle = 4·.56·sin(swingAmp)·(1 + run·1.1)):
- Walk, 4.2 m/s: 6.8 steps/s, step 0.61 m, foot travels back 0.65 m per stance. Matched.
- Sprint, 6.8 m/s (Shift): the ×2.1 'flight' factor makes each step 1.52 m, but a leg swinging ±0.70 rad only sweeps 0.76 m. There is no real flight phase: runBob is ±3.5 cm and the feet stay down. So every planted foot slides forward about 0.76 m (50%). The cadence also drops from 6.8 to 4.5 steps/s at the moment the player presses sprint.
- Slow movement, about 2 m/s (heavy carry, thick cable at 0.65×, rope pull): the hip angle is scaled by `amount` (line 68) but the cycle length isn't. About 46% slip.

Sprinting is the slingshot verb (overstretch, then Q) and the chaos route in Meeting. Pip gliding with slower legs reads as ice-skating, not a frantic dash. The sprint strip (characters-32, real time) shows long, slow scissor poses with both boots near the floor. The earlier gait work (tools/gallery/gait.*) only validated walking.
evidence: src/render/pipRig.ts:68 (hip uses swingAmp*amount, cycle uses unscaled swingAmp)
src/game.ts:318 (sprint 6.8 vs walk 4.2; carry and thick-cable slowdowns)
computed: walk 6.8 steps/s slip -5%; sprint 4.5 steps/s slip +50%; 2 m/s slip +46%
findings.fix: In pipRig.ts: compute the cycle from the amplitude actually used, `const amp=swingAmp*amount; cycle=4*.56*Math.sin(Math.max(.15,amp))` with no `(1+run*1.1)` term. Then let the cadence rise with speed (for example, cap the stride at 0.8 m per step and let frequency take the rest: `cycle=Math.min(cycle,1.6)`), so the sprint becomes about 8.5 steps/s with a bigger forward lean (already +.16) and a longer arm pump. If a flight phase is wanted, raise the body by `run*.08*Math.abs(sin)` and lift both knees during the flight half, so the 'extra' distance happens in the air. Keep walking as it is.
findings.verify: Add a tools/debug/gait-slip.mjs (or extend tools/debug/gait.mjs) that steps the rig at 60 Hz for v = 2, 4.2, 6.8 and records the world x of the lower boot while it is in contact. Slip must be under 10% of step length at every speed, and sprint cadence must be at least walk cadence. Retake characters-32 with rt.mjs (s4.mjs).
findings.verify_reason: Reran the numbers from src/render/pipRig.ts:48-52,68. Walk at 4.2 m/s (amount 1, run 0): swingAmp .58, cycle 1.23 m, 6.8 steps/s, 0.61 m step against a 0.64 m stance sweep, so it matches. Sprint at 6.8 m/s (run 1): swingAmp .70, cycle 3.03 m including the ×2.1 term, 4.5 steps/s, 1.52 m step against about 0.75 m of sweep, so about 50% slip with no airborne phase (runBob ±.035, line 56). At 2 m/s, hip amplitude .225 against a cycle of .97 gives about 47% slip. The strip characters-32 is too occluded and irregularly timed to show the slide clearly, so this verdict rests on the deterministic code math. It is a gait polish issue, not one that noticeably hurts fun or teaching, so I lowered it to P2.
extra_evidence: src/game.ts:318 (speed 6.8 sprint / 4.2 walk; carry and thick-cable divisors)
findings.fix_correction: Dropping the (1+run*1.1) term and using the amplitude actually applied (swingAmp*amount) is right for sprinting. Applied as written at low speed, it gives cycle≈0.5 m at 2 m/s, which is about 8 steps/s of tiny scurrying steps. Scale the amplitude more gently so stride and cadence share the speed change, for example `amp=swingAmp*Math.sqrt(amount)` used for both the hip (line 68) and the cycle. Keep Math.max(.4,cycle) and the cap Math.min(cycle,1.6).

findings.title: Pip can't emote: one fixed smile, mostly hidden under the hard-hat brim at the game camera
findings.problem: Pip's face is a fixed set of GLB parts: two small ink eyes (7 cm tall), cheeks and a torus smile. The rig's only facial animation is a blink (eye scale y). Straining at the cable's limit, being slingshotted, landing, alarm, the fail card and the win push-in all show the same calm smile (characters-16, -18, -63, -64b). The brim, radius 0.36 m and shifted 6 cm forward, overhangs the face by about 15 cm only 8 cm above the eyes. At the default pitch the eyes are 2–3 px under a shadowed brim (characters-40b), and walking toward the camera the face disappears entirely: only the helmet and lamp are visible (characters-30b). Good Job's comedy comes from body language. Here the coworkers get mood geometry (calm, happy, sleepy, alarm), but the hero is the least expressive character on screen. That noticeably flattens the slapstick the design depends on (DR-03, DR-11), and the face is listed as a required readable feature in ART R10.1 ('round face with eyes, cheeks and smile visible from the front at zoom ≤ 20').
evidence: tools/create_assets.py:61-62 (Helmet z1.59; HelmetBrim r .36 shifted -.06 = forward)
src/render/pipRig.ts:88-89 (blink is the only face change)
findings.fix: 1) In tools/create_assets.py, shrink the brim's forward overhang: `cylinder('HelmetBrim',(0,-.02,1.53),.33,.035,...)`. Enlarge the eyes to (.045,.025,.06) at z 1.42, and add two alternative mouth parts: 'HeadMouthO' (torus r .03, a full ring, ink) and 'HeadMouthGrit' (flat rbox .09×.025, white with an ink outline), plus 'HeadBrow{L,R}' (ink capsules .05 long) hidden by default. Regenerate public/models/pip.glb. 2) In pipRig.ts, collect these parts like `eyes`. Add a `face` state from PipState: `strain` > .85 → grit mouth, brows angled down and in; airborne > .3 or just released the slingshot → O mouth and eyes scaled 1.3; landing squash → eyes squeezed (scale y .5) for 0.15 s; `won` → big grin (smile scale 1.4) and eyes as arcs (scale y .35). 3) Tilt the hat back 0.12 rad (hat.rotation.x base) so the eyes clear the brim at the default pitch.
findings.verify: Retake characters-40b (game camera, meeting start) and characters-30b. Eyes and mouth must be visible, at 6 px or more for the pair of eyes, at the default zoom. Retake characters-16 (strain), -18 (release) and -64 (win). Each must show a different face.
findings.verify_reason: Code: the only facial change in the rig is the blink. Eye scale y is set at src/render/pipRig.ts:91-92, the mouth is a single fixed torus (tools/create_assets.py:59), and nothing reads strain, release or win for the face. Screenshots: in characters-40b at the game camera the eyes are a couple of pixels under the brim, and in characters-30b, walking toward the camera, the face is mostly hidden under the hat. Two corrections to severity: the face is clearly readable at zoom 9 (characters-01-crop), and the default camera sits behind Pip most of the time (the next-but-three finding argues exactly that), so body language matters more than the face. Lowered to P2.
findings.fix_correction: Don't add a separate base tilt to hat.rotation.x. pipRig.ts:96 overwrites it every frame with `this.hat.rotation.set(this.hatTilt.x,0,this.hatTilt.y)`, so put the offset there: `this.hat.rotation.set(this.hatTilt.x-.12,0,this.hatTilt.y)`. Negative x tips the brim up and back for a model facing +z. The rest of the fix (extra mouth and brow parts toggled by strain, air, land and won, and a smaller brim overhang in create_assets.py:62) is fine. It needs public/models/pip.glb regenerated in Blender.

findings.title: REGRESSION-check DR-65 still open: carried crate floats ahead of the mitts at head height and tilted; the arcade tray stands vertical beside the helmet
findings.problem:
Light props are driven toward a point 1.05 m ahead of Pip at p.y+0.55, which is about 1.33 m above the feet: head height, not chest. Only linear velocity and angular velocity are set; there is no orientation target, so the prop keeps whatever tilt it had when grabbed. Meanwhile the arms reach forward to about 0.5 m at shoulder height. Result:
- The crate hangs about 0.3 m beyond the mitts, tilted about 25°, at face height. From the default rear camera it covers Pip's head (characters-21, -21b, -27).
- The arcade resistor tray is carried rolled about 30° off the right mitt and, from behind, reads as a vertical slab beside the helmet (characters-81, -82). That is ART F16 / research-art-46, not fixed.

The carry is the second most common pose in the game. It looks like telekinesis and hides the hero.
evidence: src/game.ts:331 (target y=p.y+.55, ahead=1.05; setAngvel 0, no rotation target)
src/render/pipRig.ts:74 (light carry arms at -1.45, no elbow fold to meet the item)
findings.fix: In src/game.ts:331, for non-heavy props compute `ahead=.32+kind.size[2]/2` (front of chest plus half depth) and `y=p.y-.78+1.0+kind.size[1]*.3`, so the item centre sits at about 1.0–1.1 m, chest height. Drive orientation each step: `const want=new T.Quaternion().setFromEuler(new T.Euler(0,this.heading,0)); b.setRotation(slerp(current,want,.25))` (or set angvel from the quaternion error). For flat kinds (size[1] < .2: tray, strip, splitter, paper, bridge), use the same level target. In pipRig.ts:74, use reach -1.25 for light items and fold the elbows to -.45 so the mitts meet the item's sides (lz/rz from the item's half width, passed in as `carryWidth` on PipState).
findings.verify: Retake characters-20/21/22 (s3.mjs) and characters-81/82 (s10.mjs). The item must touch both mitts, be level within 5°, and its bounding box must stay clear of a sphere of r 0.3 at y 1.4 (Pip's head), per the DR-65 check.
findings.verify_reason: Code: src/game.ts:331 drives light props to p.y+.55 (the player body is at y≈0.77 and the feet at p.y-.78, so the target is about 1.32 m, head height), 1.05 m ahead, with angvel zeroed and no orientation target. Screenshots: in characters-21 the crate floats beyond the mitts at helmet height, tilted about 25°. In characters-22 it covers Pip's torso. In characters-82 the arcade tray stands nearly upright beside the helmet, and in characters-81 it hangs off the right mitt, rolled. This is DR-65 / ART F16 and is not fixed.
extra_evidence: snapshot player.y = 0.77 (verify-characters v1 run), so target y = 1.32 m

findings.title: Overstretch pull pose swings the plug over the shoulder into the helmet
findings.problem: When strain passes about 0.85 (pull > .5), the right arm snaps to rotation.x = +2.45 rad. That swings the glove up and behind the shoulder, to about (0.39, 1.5, -0.32) m. The plug, about 0.25 m long, then sits against the side and back of the head, with the prongs into the brim (characters-16b). From the default rear camera it reads as a yellow box stuck on Pip's ear while the red cable drops vertically down his back (characters-16). The pose is meant to read as 'hauling over the shoulder', which is a good comedic idea, but the plug clips the helmet. The cable also ends at the head, so the strain gradient visually runs into Pip's skull. ART R10.3 / DR-65: never intersecting the head or helmet.
findings.fix: Change the haul pose to a two-handed tug-of-war lean. Right arm rx = -.6 (forward-down) with rz -.25, left arm lx = -.9 reaching for the cable, elbows -.6, and keep the torso lean -.32 (pipRig.ts:63) plus knees bent .3 for a dug-in stance. If the over-shoulder pose is kept, cap rx at 1.9, add rz = -.7 so the hand moves out to x ≈ .6, away from the brim (r .36), and rotate the plug so its prongs point back along the cable.
findings.verify: Retake characters-16/16b/17 (s2.mjs). The plug's bounding box must not intersect a sphere of r 0.36 around (0,1.45,0) in Pip's local space. A crop must show a clear gap between the plug and the brim.
findings.verify_reason: Code: src/render/pipRig.ts:75 sets rx=2.45 once pull>.5, which is strain above 0.85, and the plug is attached to the hand under elbows[1] (line 40). In characters-16 and the 16b crop, the yellow plug sits against the side and back of the head with its prongs into the skull and brim. The red, strained cable drops straight down Pip's back from there. This breaks the 'never intersect the head' part of DR-65.

findings.title: REGRESSION-check DR-64 (ART F9) still open: plinth soles, a ridge that reads as a fin or ears, and arms that merge into a cape
findings.problem:
public/models/pip.glb hasn't changed since commit 1649a1e, and all three F9 artefacts are visible in the new 6-angle sheet:
- **Soles:** grey bevelled slabs (0.26 × 0.42 m) stick out past the round ink boots on every side. Pip stands on little skates or plinths (characters-09, all six angles; characters-60b; -21b).
- **Ridge:** the 0.48 m bevelled box on the dome pokes above the helmet at front and back. From behind and above it reads as a tab or 'ears' (characters-04 a180, characters-16b). At the game camera it looks like a crack down the helmet (characters-40b).
- **Arms:** the upper-arm ellipsoids (0.22 × 0.24 × 0.54 m, pivot ±.39) sit flush against the 0.68 m-wide torso. Their tops bulge up beside the chin like shoulder pads or wings in the front view (characters-01, -40b), and from behind the arms and torso form one wide blue mass (characters-04, -83, -85).

Pip is on screen 100% of the time, so these read as modelling errors.
findings.fix: In tools/create_assets.py: replace the sole cube with `sphere(f'Boot{n}Sole',(s*.17,-.08,.04),(.135,.225,.035),grey)`, which sits entirely under the boot. Shorten the ridge to `cube('HelmetRidge',(0,0,1.70),(.03,.16,.03),...)`, or replace it with a raised band `torus('HelmetBand',(0,0,1.55),.30,.018,yellow)`. Move the arms to x ±.43 with scale (.095,.105,.24) and centre z .86, so the arm top stays below the shoulder line (1.10). Add a navy shoulder seam `torus(f'Arm{n}Seam',(s*.42,0,1.06),.08,.02,navy,rot=(0,math.pi/2,0))`. Update src/render/pipRig.ts:37 arm pivots to ±.43 and the elbows (line 38) to match. Regenerate public/models/pip.glb.
findings.verify: Rerun mockups/review5/tools/characters/s1.mjs and retake the 6-angle sheet. No grey visible beyond the boot silhouette from any angle. No fin above the dome from behind. A visible notch between arm and torso in the a0 and a180 crops.
findings.verify_reason: In the characters-09 6-angle sheet and the characters-04 crop: grey bevelled sole slabs stick out around both ink boots at every angle; the HelmetRidge tab pokes above the dome front and back; in the front view the arm tops bulge above the shoulder line like pads; and from behind the arms and torso merge into one blue mass. Generator lines match: create_assets.py:63 ridge, :71 sole cube, :74 arm at ±.39. git log shows public/models/pip.glb and tools/create_assets.py last changed in 1649a1e, so the DR-64 / F9 items are still open.
extra_evidence: mockups/review5/shots/verify-characters-17-title-right-edge-sheet.jpg (soles plainly visible as grey plinths on the title hero too)
findings.fix_correction: Moving the arm pivots to ±.43 in pipRig.ts means changing line 34 (arms) and line 35 (elbows), not 37/38. The hand anchor on line 40 should be checked against the new glove position too.

findings.title: Pip's back is a blank blue egg, and the default camera shows his back most of the time

The back views (characters-04 crop, characters-09 bottom row, verify-characters-18 panel 1) show a plain blue back with only the belt torus. The default camera looks at this side most of the time.

findings.title: Seated blobs push through their chair backrests and sink 17 cm into the seat
findings.problem: The seated blob is placed at the chair's centre. Its capsule (r 0.33, centre y 0.9 with the 0.35 lift) reaches 0.33 m back, but the backrest's front face is only 0.215 m behind the seat centre, so about 11 cm of body passes through the back pad. From behind, an orange or purple 'tooth' of the blob shows through the backrest (characters-41c, -43b). The capsule bottom is at 0.395 m while the seat pad top is at about 0.565 m, so the body also sinks about 0.17 m into the cushion. The blobs also yaw their whole body to watch Pip while the chair stays fixed (game.ts:424-428), so the clipping sweeps through the armrests as they turn. The player orbits (AGENTS 8) and passes behind these desks on the clean route to the boardroom.
evidence: src/props/prefabs.ts:70-71 (seat pad top bottom+.55; backrest at z -.26, depth .09 → front face -.215)
src/game.ts:424-428 (seated blobs rotate their group yaw to watch Pip and fidget)
findings.fix: In addNpc (src/game.ts:128), for seated blobs set `body.position.y=.52` (the seat top minus a 4 cm cushion sink) and offset the body 0.13 m forward along the chair's facing: `body.position.z=.13` in group space, with the group yaw set to the chair's rotation. Scale the seated body z to .9. In render(), turn the seated blob's watch by rotating `npc.body` (yaw clamped to ±0.6 rad) instead of the group, so the blob looks round within the chair rather than spinning through it.
findings.verify: Retake characters-41c/43b/44b (s5.mjs). No blob colour may show through the backrest from behind or from the side. Optionally, check `audit()` with seated blobs included.
findings.verify_reason: Geometry checks out. The chair back is at z -.26, .09 deep, so its front face is at -.215 (src/props/prefabs.ts:71). The blob capsule has r .33, z scale .96, about 0.32 m deep (src/render/actors.ts:32, not :24), and it is centred on the chair, so about 10 cm of blob passes through the back. The capsule bottom is at .35+.55-.175-.33≈.395 m, while the seat pad top is about .59 m (chair centre .5, bottom .025, pad at +.55), so the blob sinks about 19 cm. Screenshots: blob colour shows through the backrest from behind (characters-41c purple through orange, characters-43b yellow through orange). Seated blobs also yaw their whole group to watch Pip while the chair stays still (src/game.ts:424-428).
findings.fix_correction: The capsule geometry is at src/render/actors.ts:32. With the seat top at about .59, the body y that puts the capsule bottom about 4 cm into the cushion is about .50 (.55-.045), close to the .52 proposed. Fine as given.

findings.title: Alarm pose squashes blobs flat while the sweat drop and "!" float detached above them
findings.problem: When alarmed, the body is squashed to y 0.72 and xz 1.28 (`duck`), so a standing blob's head drops from 1.06 m to about 0.76 m. The sweat sprite stays at a fixed 1.02 m and the bubble at 1.55 m on the unsquashed group. The drop hangs about 0.26 m in the air above and beside the head, and the "!" floats about 0.8 m up (characters-48c: the purple blob is a flat dome with its startled eyes squeezed onto the top, and its sweat drop hangs in space). For seated blobs the squash turns them into a mound with eyes on the crown (characters-90). It reads as being stepped on, or as a macaron or bun shape (DR-52), rather than startled. Good Job's laughs come from coworkers recoiling or jumping. The startled mesh's raised arm nubs (rz -2.3) are also hidden by the squash.
findings.fix: Replace the squash with a recoil hop in src/game.ts:426-429. Over the first 0.15 s of alarm, stretch (scale y 1.15, xz .93) and lift the body by `Math.sin(age*Math.PI/.3)*.25`. Then settle to a slight lean away from the impact: rotate body.x by .2 toward −(impact direction), which needs the alarm point stored on the npc. Parent the sweat and bubble sprites to `npc.body` (not `g`), or update them each frame to `npc.body.position.y+1.1*npc.body.scale.y`, so they ride on the head.
findings.verify: Retake characters-48/48c (s6.mjs) and characters-90 (s11.mjs). The sweat drop must touch the head silhouette, the "!" must sit 0.2–0.4 m above the head, and the blob must be taller during the first 0.3 s, not flatter.
findings.verify_reason: Code: when alarmed, duck=.72 (src/game.ts:426) and body.scale=(1.28,.72,1.28) (line 429), which puts the head top at about .76 m for a standing blob. The sweat sprite sits at a fixed 1.02 m (line 131) and the bubble at 1.55 m (line 132), both on the unscaled group. Screenshots: in characters-48c the purple blob is a flat dome with its eyes on top and the sweat drop hanging well above it. In characters-90 the seated alarmed blobs are squat mounds.
findings.fix_correction: Don't parent the sprites to npc.body. Body scale is non-uniform (1.28/.72/1.28, or the 1.15/.93 stretch), and a T.Sprite inherits its parent's world scale, so the drop and the '!' would be squashed and stretched with the body. Keep them on the group and set their y each frame from the body: `sweat.position.y=npc.body.position.y+(.55+.505)*npc.body.scale.y-.05`, and the bubble about 0.3 m above that.

findings.title: "!" bubbles draw through everything at 0.7 m and pile up over desks and near Pip
findings.problem: Each alarm bubble is a 0.7 m sprite with depthTest:false and renderOrder 9, which overshoots to 0.91 m. One thrown chair startled 8 seated coworkers, and four or five big white discs immediately covered the desk cluster, a monitor and the space right beside Pip's helmet, drawn over the pillar and the desks in front of them (characters-90, -91). DR-04 wants the bubble visible, which it is. But stacked at this size they become the highest-contrast shapes in the frame, above Pip and the goal (DR-43), and with depthTest off one can sit on top of Pip whenever a startled blob is between Pip and the camera.
findings.fix: Set bubble scale .45 (pop to 1.2×) and turn depthTest back on, with a small depth offset (polygonOffset, or y +0.2) so it isn't hidden by its own blob. Limit visible bubbles to the 3 nearest the impact, and give the rest only the sweat drop. Fade bubbles whose screen position falls within 80 px of Pip's head, using opacity .35.
findings.verify: Retake characters-90 (s11.mjs). At most 3 bubbles, none overlapping Pip, and Pip plus the thrown chair still read first in a greyscale squint.
findings.verify_reason: In characters-90 four large white '!' discs cover the desk cluster and monitors, and one sits right next to Pip's helmet. They draw over the desks because the SpriteMaterial has depthTest:false and renderOrder 9 (src/game.ts:132), with a pop to 1.3× (line 430, scale .7*s).
findings.fix_correction: Keep depthTest:false. Showing the '!' through desks and clutter is what DR-04 asks for, and turning depth testing on would hide bubbles behind monitors and pillars in a dense room. Shrink them instead (scale about .45, pop to 1.2×), cap the visible count at the 3 nearest the impact (the rest get sweat only), and fade any bubble whose projected position is within about 80 px of Pip's head projection.

findings.title: Throw and slingshot release have no body animation
findings.problem: Q while carrying applies an impulse to the prop, and Q while holding the plug calls releasePlug. Neither tells the rig anything: PipState has no `throwing` or `released` field. Pip's arms just ease from the carry or haul pose back to idle while the crate flies off his head (characters-24, -18). The two chaos verbs that AGENTS 4 and 5 build the comedy on have no anticipation, follow-through or recoil. Even a 0.25 s overhead heave, or a stumble backwards when the overstretched cable is let go, would sell the physics. Hard landings already get a squash (game.ts:323), so the pattern exists.
findings.fix: Add `throwAt:number` and `releaseAt:number` to PipState (set to this.time in game.ts:183 and in releasePlug). In pipRig.update, for 0.3 s after a throw: both arms swing from -2.6 (overhead) to -0.6 with the torso pitching forward .25, plus a small hop. For 0.4 s after a slingshot release with strain above .9: lean back -.35, take a backward step (body.position.z -.15), flail the arms out (lz/rz ±1.2) and use the O-mouth face from the expression finding. Optionally add a 60 ms hitstop on release (this.hitstop already exists).
findings.verify: Retake characters-24 and characters-18 with real-time capture (rt.mjs), 3 frames at 60 ms intervals after Q. The arms must be overhead or flailing in frame 1 and settling by frame 3.
findings.verify_reason: Code: the throw at src/game.ts:183 is only `this.held=undefined; p.body.applyImpulse(...)` plus a tone, and the Q-on-plug path calls releasePlug(). PipState (src/render/pipRig.ts:6-11) has no throw or release field, so the rig just eases back to idle. Hard landings do get a squash (src/game.ts:323), so the pattern exists. This is a missing animation, polish-level.

findings.title: REGRESSION-check DR-60 still open: the arcade play-tester is a realistic human kid
findings.problem: The concept and ART R6.3 allow one humanoid (Pip), with everyone else a blob. The arcade play-tester standing at the cabinet next to the bench is a small human: a skin-tone sphere head, brown hair cap, orange shirt cylinder, blue cylinder legs and skin-tone hands (characters-83, -85). It sits in the frame of every bench approach, is unoutlined and thin-limbed next to the chunky cast, and breaks the one-character-language rule. It is also a second, smaller humanoid beside Pip, which muddies Pip's silhouette as 'the human' (DR-43).
evidence: src/stations/arcade/station.ts:225-231 (cyl legs, cyl body, sphere(.13) head '#f2c49b', hair, arms)
findings.fix: Replace the kid with a small blob: `blob(BLOBC[4],'happy',['cap'])` scaled to 0.75 and placed at the same k.position. Drive the 'hop while working / slump when dark' animation through the blob's body scale (stretch when hopping, squash .8 and use the 'sleepy' mesh when slumped). Keep the solid() collider. Remove the '#f2c49b' parts.
findings.verify: Retake characters-83 (s10.mjs). `grep -n "#f2c49b" src` must return nothing outside tools/create_assets.py.
findings.verify_reason: Code: src/stations/arcade/station.ts:225-231 builds the play tester from cylinder legs, a cylinder torso, a '#f2c49b' skin-tone sphere head, a brown hair cap and skin-tone hands. In characters-83 the small human stands at the cabinet left of the bench. This violates DR-60's one character language. On priority: the kid is about 100 px tall at the edge of the bench approach and doesn't affect playing, solving or understanding, so as an art-style inconsistency it fits P2 polish. RULES.md lists DR-60 as 'Known ... P1'; whoever sets the final priority may choose to follow the rulebook.

findings.title: Pip's outline is thin and light: luma about 106, 1–2 px, even at zoom 9
findings.problem: Sampled across the helmet and arm edges in the zoom-9 front shot (Pip about 300 px tall), the outline pixel is rgb(101,104,135), luma 106, and only 1–2 px wide. DR-56 asks for ink of luma 70 or less at 2–3 px. At the game camera (characters-40b), Pip's silhouette against the blue-grey meeting carpet relies on the yellow helmet and ring, because the outline barely separates the blue overalls (luma 132, hue 195°) from the floor (luma 158). The same applies to the blobs, which share the outline pass. The concept's chunky toon look depends on a dark contour around the hero.
evidence: mockups/review5/shots/characters-01-pip-idle-zoom9-a0.jpg (rows y=320,420: min luma 106 at the silhouette)
findings.fix: In src/render/toon.ts:77, set the outline colour to [.07,.075,.12] (about #12131f in linear, which displays near rgb(52,54,76) after ACES and sRGB) and thickness .0055. Give Pip's materials their own `userData.outlineParameters={thickness:.007}` (set when traversing the GLB in game.ts:156), so the hero gets the heaviest line.
findings.verify: Rerun s1.mjs and resample the same rows. The minimum silhouette luma must be 70 or less and 2 px or wider. Retake characters-40b.
findings.verify_reason: I resampled characters-01-pip-idle-zoom9-a0.jpg myself. The silhouette edge pixels on row 320 (x 651, 779-780) and row 420 (x 637-638, 797-799) measure luma 106-110, rgb(101,104,135), and are 1-2 px wide. The interior ink (eyes, boots) is darker, luma about 48. This matches DR-56's Known values and fails the ≤70 luma, 2-3 px rule.
findings.fix_correction: The colour values are wrong. The outline is not tone-mapped: [.13,.135,.2] linear shows as about (101,104,135), which is plain linear-to-sRGB. So [.07,.075,.12] would show as about rgb(74,77,97), luma about 78, which still fails. To reach the target rgb(52,54,76) (#34364c, luma ≤70), set defaultColor to about [.035,.037,.072] at src/render/toon.ts:77. Raising defaultThickness from .0036 to about .0055, with the hero override userData.outlineParameters={thickness:.007} on Pip's materials, is fine.

findings.title: Pip blends into the blue coworkers and the blue meeting carpet at the game camera
findings.problem: Pip's overalls (median rgb(74,153,181), hue 195°, luma 132) are close to the blue blob hue '#5b9cf0' (rgb(95,152,209), hue 210°, luma 141). Pip is also only 26 luma above the blue-grey carpet (158). In the Meeting start frame there are 3–4 blue blobs near Pip, and at 120 px tall Pip is distinguished mainly by the yellow hat and ring (characters-40, -40b). evidence: src/levels/lunch.ts:30 (a '#5b9cf0' blob next to Pip's spawn)
measured medians: Pip overalls luma 132 hue 195; blue blob luma 141 hue 210; floor luma 158
findings.fix: Either push Pip's overalls to a deeper, more saturated cobalt in tools/create_assets.py (blue material about (.05,.30,.75) linear) for a 40+ luma gap below the floor, or drop '#5b9cf0' from BLOBC (src/render/kit.ts:10) and the lunch spot (src/levels/lunch.ts:30) in favour of a coral or lime, so no coworker shares Pip's hue family. The thicker hero outline in the outline finding helps as well.

The nearby blue blobs are rgb(96,153-156,209-215), luma 142-144, hue 209°. The gap to the floor is about 27 luma, and the hue sits within about 10° of a BLOBC colour (src/render/kit.ts:10 '#5b9cf0'). findings.title: Win push-in under the lamp washes Pip out
findings.problem: The Playground win frames Pip right under the lit floor lamp. Its point light and bloom push Pip's overalls from rgb(92,172,206) to rgb(117,169,173), a desaturated teal, and the helmet goes nearly white. The face and outline lose contrast just as the camera pushes in for the hero moment (characters-63, -64, -64b). The win shot does contain Pip and the machine (QA 10 / DR-11 is fixed here), but the hero reads paler than the confetti.
findings.fix: Exclude Pip from the lamp's light-up (set the lamp PointLight's distance to 1.8 m, or lower its intensity by 40%), or move the push-in focus (winFocus, src/game.ts:398) so Pip stands 1.2 m to the camera side of the lamp. Make sure the bloom threshold (1.3) is not exceeded by Pip's lit albedo.
findings.verify: Retake characters-64 (s8.mjs). Pip's overall pixels must keep a saturation within 15% of the start shot.
findings.verify_reason: In characters-64, at the win push-in, Pip stands under the lit lamp: the overalls turn pale teal and the helmet goes nearly white, while the confetti stays saturated. The lightUp at src/levels/decor.ts:93-94 adds a 3 m warm glow sprite plus pointLamp(intensity 10, distance 9) right above Pip's spot. The cited cause, src/game.ts:350 calling lightUp, is right.
extra_evidence: src/levels/decor.ts:93-94 (glow 3 m sprite; pointLamp intensity 10, distance 9)
findings.fix_correction: Don't cut the PointLight distance to 1.8 m. The lamp lighting up the room is the visible payoff of the win (DR-11 flash), and a 1.8 m light would barely reach the floor from the bulb. Lower the pointLamp intensity (10 → about 6) and shrink or lift the glow sprite (glow size 3 → about 1.8, src/levels/decor.ts:93), or shift winFocus (src/game.ts:398) so Pip stands about 1.2 m to the camera side of the cone.

findings.title: Coworkers only sit in the Meeting; the Lunch crowd stands beside empty benches, and the chef faces away

Mark the corridor crowd spots `seated:true` at the bench seat positions, with the seat height read from the bench prefab instead of the fixed .35. The corridor benches are static decor at x -4.2 and -2.6, z 9.45, seat top about .51 (src/levels/decor.ts:194), and the crowd spots (-3.8,9) and (-2.4,8.9) sit about 0.5 m in front of them (src/levels/lunch.ts:30). In characters-70 and -73 the blobs stand beside or behind the empty benches. The chef has yaw 2.8 (lunch.ts:29) and is seen side-on or from behind in characters-71.

Move the crowd spots onto the bench centres (x -4.2/-2.6, z 9.45), mark them seated, and lift body y to about .47 (seat .51 minus the .045 capsule offset). findings.title: Pip disappears entirely at the bench; nothing of him is in the bench view
findings.room: arcade, garage, qfn, observatory, spectrum (station benches)
findings.problem: On E at a bench, the avatar and ring are hidden (`avatar.visible=!this.atBench`). The station camera then shows the tabletop with no hands, and blocks teleport into the chain (characters-84). The over-shoulder framing in the comment never shows Pip's shoulder. Benches are where players spend most of a station job, so for minutes at a time the physical-comedy hero is absent and the 'play by doing' acts (pick, place, flip) are abstract button presses. This isn't a bug, but it is a missed character moment.

Alternatively, keep Pip visible at the near edge of the frame (lower-left, back view, out-of-focus scale) and play a small 'reach' anim on each act.
findings.verify: Retake characters-84 after `act('pick',47)` and `act('slot',0)`. A mitt must be visible moving between the bin and slot A.
findings.verify_reason: Code: src/game.ts:416 sets avatar.visible=!this.atBench and hides the ring. The bench view (characters-84) shows only the tabletop, with no mitts or hands. The comment at line 415 says over-the-shoulder, but no shoulder is in frame. This is a design suggestion rather than a bug, so P2.

The raised glove reaches x≈1390-1440 and touches or crosses the right edge depending on phase. In the original characters-80 it is cut off. notes.models: Pip (public/models/pip.glb from tools/create_assets.py) has the right parts and colour language: yellow hard hat with a lamp, blue overalls with front straps, belt, buckle and wrench, white mitts with thumbs, ink boots. At zoom 9 he reads as a friendly chibi technician that fits the concept, and the hat lamp is a nice touch. The three ART F9 artefacts are all still present: grey plinth soles, the ridge fin, and arms like shoulder pads that form a cape. The back is blank, the face is small and fixed, and the brim covers it at the game camera. Outlines are thin and light (luma about 106). The coworker blobs are the strongest models in the game: one capsule, big eyes with glints, blush, mood mouths, and accessories (headphones, glasses, cap, mug, tie, bun, sprout, tuft) that sit correctly with no floating or clipping in any shot I checked (characters-41b, -47, -48c, -52b). The mug held by an arm nub works. The model problems are in how blobs meet the world: seated blobs pass through backrests and hover once their chair is taken, and the alarm squash detaches the sweat and bubble. The arcade's human kid still breaks the one-character language.
notes.playability: Pip's controls and poses are readable at the game camera thanks to the hat and the soft ring, and none of the character models blocked play. The carry placement does affect play. The crate is held at head height 1.05 m ahead and blocks Pip's head from the default rear camera, and the tilted tray reads as unstable. In the Lunch room the thick-cable dolly parks against Pip's hip, the cable runs through his body, and the reel occludes him when the camera orbits. Seated blobs aren't attached to their chairs, so the 'Grab the chair' prompt at every Meeting desk leaves a hovering coworker. That's a visual soft fail, not a play blocker. Review tooling note: in ?manual, drive.advance(s) renders once at the end with dt = 1/60, so animateRig sees the whole interval's displacement as a 1/60 s move: speed clamps to 9 and the pose jumps. Gait judgements need real-time capture (characters/rt.mjs, used for strips 30–33) or advance(1/60) loops.
notes.fun: The world reacts: one thrown chair startled 8 seated coworkers with "!" bubbles and sweat, and the coffee-corner blobs flinch (DR-04 passes on timing). The win pose (arms up, hopping, confetti, coworkers cheering) is cheerful. The comedy is held back by Pip himself. He has one face. Throwing and the slingshot release have no body animation. The sprint, the main chaos verb, skates with slower legs than walking. The alarm reaction squashes coworkers flat instead of making them recoil. The pieces that would make the chaos funny are missing: strain grit, a release flail, an overhead heave, coworkers hopping back, and coworkers falling off yanked chairs. They are small rig and geometry additions on top of a solid base.
notes.teaching: Out of scope for this dimension, apart from one point. The cable's strain colour reads correctly in Pip's haul pose (white at the reel to red at the hand, characters-16). But the over-shoulder haul ends the red section at Pip's head, so the 'hot end' looks attached to his skull rather than to the plug in his glove. Fixing the haul pose and the cable clearance keeps the strain lesson on the cable.
notes.clarity: Pip is findable at every camera thanks to the yellow helmet and ring. His blue overalls sit close to the '#5b9cf0' coworker hue and only about 26 luma above the Meeting carpet, so with blue blobs nearby the helmet does all the work (DR-43). Alarm bubbles at 0.7 m with depthTest off pile up and become the loudest shapes in the frame after one chaos event. The face, the main expressive and clarity cue for a character, is effectively invisible at the default camera.
